items.title: Analytic KAM data: angular tori, action-angle neighbourhoods, Fourier cutoffs and Diophantine frequency labels
items.statement: Throughout, fix an integer $n\ge1$. The space $\mathbb R^n$ is read through [[rem-complex-euclidean-space-dictionary]] and $\mathbb C^n$ carries the polydisc geometry of [[def-balls-and-polydiscs-in-complex-euclidean-space]]. All norms below are supremum norms: for $z\in\mathbb C^m$, $$|z|_\infty:=\max_{1\le i\le m}|z_i|,\qquad |z|_1:=\sum_{i=1}^m|z_i| .$$ **Angular torus.** Let $\mathbb Z$ be the integers ([[def-integers]]). Write $k=(k_1,\dots,k_n)\in\mathbb Z^n$, $|k|_1=|k_1|+\dots+|k_n|$, and let $(2\pi\mathbb Z)^n:=\{2\pi k:k\in\mathbb Z^n\}\subseteq\mathbb R^n$. On $\mathbb R^n$ define the relation $\vartheta\sim\vartheta'$ by $\vartheta-\vartheta'\in(2\pi\mathbb Z)^n$. This is an equivalence relation, and the **angular torus** is the quotient set $$\mathbb T^n:=(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)^n:=\mathbb R^n/\!\sim$$ with the quotient topology ([[def-quotient-topology]], [[def-product-topology]]), and canonical projection $\pi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb T^n$, which is continuous ([[def-continuous-map-top]]). A map $f:\mathbb R^n\to X$ is **$2\pi$-periodic** if ...
items.strategy: Define the KAM analytic data, domains, Fourier calculus and Diophantine labels with explicit quantifiers and conventions; no existence claim and no proof obligation is smuggled into the definition.

references.title: Jürgen Pöschel, A Lecture on the Classical KAM Theorem, arXiv:0908.2234, §2 (the domain $D_{r,s}$, the parameter neighbourhood $O_h$, the sup-norm and the Diophantine sets $\mathcal D_\alpha$), PDF pp. 8-13.

Rafael de la Llave, A Tutorial on KAM Theory (AMS Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 69, revised version), §3.1 (analytic preliminaries and quasi-periodic data), §3.3 (Diophantine properties and the resonant strips) and §3.5 (geometric structures: symplectic forms and Lagrangian submanifolds), printed pp. 24-31, 32-36 and 40-49.

items.title: Fourier decay, Cauchy derivative bounds, lattice shell counts and the exponential small-divisor sums on action-angle neighbourhoods
items.strategy: direct; shift the Fourier contours into the complex strip with Goursat's rectangle theorem, identify the series by Fejer uniqueness, bound derivatives by one-variable Cauchy estimates, and evaluate the lattice sums by shell counting and geometric comparison.

references.title: Jürgen Pöschel, A Lecture on the Classical KAM Theorem, arXiv:0908.2234, §1-§2 (contour shift for Fourier coefficients $|g_k|\le|g|_s e^{-s|k|_1}$; lattice shell estimate $\sum_k|k|^\tau e^{-\sigma|k|_1}\le C\sigma^{-\tau-n}$; Fourier truncation), PDF pp. 5-13.

Rafael de la Llave, A Tutorial on KAM Theory (AMS Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 69, revised version), §3.1 (analytic norms and Fourier coefficients) and §3.3 (Diophantine properties and the shell counts for the resonant strips), printed pp. 24-31 and 32-36.

items.title: Affine Taylor splitting in the actions and conservative Fourier truncation of a small perturbation
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, $r>0$, $s>0$, $h>0$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, let $K\ge0$, $0<\eta\le1/4$, $0<\sigma\le\min(1,s/4)$, and let $P$ be holomorphic on $D_{r,s,h}(\Omega)$ with $|P|_{r,s,h}\le\varepsilon$ ([[def-holomorphic-kam-domain-and-diophantine-labels]]). Define the **affine action-Taylor polynomial** $$Q(I,\vartheta,
u):=P(0,\vartheta,
u)+\sum_{j=1}^n \partial_{I_j}P(0,\vartheta,
u)\,I_j ,$$ and the **truncated perturbation** $R:=T_KQ$ (Fourier cutoff in $\vartheta$). Then: 1. **Taylor remainder.** $|P-Q|_{2\eta r,s,h}\le C\eta^2\varepsilon$ with a constant $C=C(n)$. 2. **Affine structure.** $Q$ and $R$ are holomorphic on $D_{r,s,h}(\Omega)$ and affine in $I$: $R(I,\vartheta,
u)=R_0(\vartheta,
u)+\sum_{j=1}^nR_j(\vartheta,
u)I_j$ with $R_0,R_j$ trigonometric polynomials in $\vartheta$ of degree at most $K$; $[R]=[Q]$ is affine in $I$, and $R-[R]$ is zero-mean. 3. **Size bounds.** $|Q|_{r,s,h}\le(n+1)\varepsilon$ and $$|R|_{r,s-2\sigma,h}\le C_n\sigma^{-n}\varepsilon,\qquad \max_j|R_j|_{r,s-2\sigma,h}\le C_n\sigma^{-n}\varepsilon/r,\qquad ...
items.strategy: direct; expand $P$ in the action variable along the segment $tI$, bound the quadratic remainder by Cauchy estimates, and truncate the Fourier series of $Q$ with the exponential tail bound.

items.title: One KAM step: the affine generator, its canonical time-one flow, and the quadratic remainder bound

references.title: Jürgen Pöschel, A Lecture on the Classical KAM Theorem, arXiv:0908.2234, §3-§4 (the generator $F$ with $\{F,N\}+\hat R=R$, the estimates $r^{-1}|F_\vartheta|+\sigma^{-1}|F_I|\le C\varepsilon/(\alpha r\sigma^{\mu})$, the time-one flow of $X_F$ and the transformed perturbation $\varepsilon_+\le C[\varepsilon/(\alpha r\sigma^{\mu})+\eta^2+K^ne^{-K\sigma}]\varepsilon$), PDF pp. 14-22.

u_+\in O_{h/4}(\Omega)$ there is exactly one $
u\in O_{h/2}(\Omega)$ with $$

references.title: Jürgen Pöschel, A Lecture on the Classical KAM Theorem, arXiv:0908.2234, §1 and §4-§5 (the real-analytic perturbation is complexified to a holomorphic function of the action-angle-parameter variables; the constructed transformations are limits of real-analytic maps), PDF pp. 5-6 and 20-27.

Rafael de la Llave, A Tutorial on KAM Theory (AMS Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 69, revised version), §3.1 (real analytic functions and their complexifications) and §6.1-§6.3 (reality of the limiting embedding when the data are real), printed pp. 24-31 and 92-110.

items.title: A two-rotor model with units: dimensionless normalisation, Diophantine measure and the conditional KAM family
items.reference: analytic-kam.md#e28; batch-14-local-construction; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: **The dimensionless model.** On the phase space $\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb T^2$ with angular variables $\theta_1,\theta_2$ read modulo $2\pi$, consider the Hamiltonian $$H(I,\theta):=\tfrac12(I_1^2+I_2^2)+\varepsilon\cos\theta_1\cos\theta_2,\qquad I=(I_1,I_2)\in\mathbb R^2,$$ so that $h(I)=\tfrac12|I|^2$ and $F(I,\theta)=\varepsilon\cos\theta_1\cos\theta_2$. This is the standard dimensionless two-rotor (two decoupled rigid rotors with a cosine coupling) and is a worked instance of [[thm-positive-measure-analytic-kam-family]]. The example is conditional mathematics: nothing below asserts that any physical rotor is governed by this model, and no empirical quantity, measurement or statistical inference occurs. **The physical reading with units.** Let $E_0$ be a chosen energy unit and let a physical two-rotor have common moment of inertia $\mathcal I>0$ and coupling energy $\lambda>0$ (both measured in their own units), with Hamiltonian $$H_{\mathrm{phys}}(p,q)=\frac{p_1^2+p_2^2}{2\mathcal I}+\lambda\cos q_1\cos q_2 .$$ With the action unit $J_0:=(\mathcal I ...
items.strategy: direct; write the dimensionless normalisation, check the data of the KAM theorem with explicit constants, estimate the Diophantine measure arithmetically, and translate the conclusion back to physical units.

references.title: Jürgen Pöschel, A Lecture on the Classical KAM Theorem, arXiv:0908.2234, §1 and §5 (the general perturbation form $H=h(p)+f_\varepsilon(p,q)$, $f_\varepsilon=\epsilon f_*(p,q,\epsilon)$, real analytic, with the standard symplectic structure; and the $\alpha^2$ smallness of the iteration); the concrete two-rotor specialisation is constructed in this example, PDF pp. 5-6 and 23-30.

Rafael de la Llave, A Tutorial on KAM Theory (AMS Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 69, revised version), §2.1-§2.2 (model examples of perturbation theory) and §3.3 (Diophantine frequencies and the measure of the resonant set), printed pp. 7-23 and 32-36.
